diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-1 Structural view of steering system
diagrams.description: Structural perspective drawing showing the complete steering system layout in relation to the front suspension and steering column assembly.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Universal joints require no lubrication. Rubber coupling isolates road vibration.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-2 Removing steering wheel
diagrams.description: Removing steering wheel using Steering Wheel Puller ST27180001 threaded into the steering wheel hub.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Do not strike end of steering column shaft with a hammer. Striking shaft will damage bearing or collapsible shaft. Be careful not to damage cancel pole.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-3 Sectional view of collapsible type steering
diagrams.description: Sectional view of the steel ball collapsible steering column showing jacket tubes, bearing, spring, bracket, and rubber coupling.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Never apply undue stress to steering column in axial direction. Do not apply bending force during installation.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-4 Removing rubber coupling bolt
diagrams.description: Removing bolt securing the steering column shaft to the rubber coupling flange.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect steering column assembly from lower joint shaft at rubber coupling by removing bolt.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-5 Removing jacket tube bracket securing bolts
diagrams.description: Location of four bolts securing jacket tube bracket to the dash panel under the dashboard.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove bolts securing jacket tube bracket to dash panel.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-6 Removing column clamp securing bolts
diagrams.description: Removing two column clamp securing bolts while supporting the steering column assembly.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Support steering column at the top portion while removing two column clamp securing bolts.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-7 Drawing out steering column assembly
diagrams.description: Withdrawing the complete steering column assembly rearward into the passenger compartment.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Draw out steering column assembly from the interior side.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-8 Loosening nut securing lower joint to pinion gear
diagrams.description: Loosening pinch bolt nut clamping the lower steering joint to the pinion gear serration.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Take lower joint assembly out by loosening nut securing lower joint to pinion gear.

diagrams.caption: Column shaft spring dimensions
diagrams.description: Inspection dimension diagram of the column shaft spring showing outer diameter and free length.
measurements_and_specs: Load x length: 30 kg (66 lb) x 15 mm (0.59 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Replace spring if damaged or weakened.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-9 Standard dimension between column clamp and the top end of lower jacket tube
diagrams.description: Measuring dimension A between column clamp and the upper edge of lower jacket tube to inspect for collapse.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: When jacket tube is crushed in a collision, dimension A becomes smaller.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-10 Standard dimension B
diagrams.description: Checking dimension B gap at the column clamp block to determine if the column has begun collapsing.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Standard B dimension is 0 mm (0 in). When jacket tube is crushed, dimension B becomes larger.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-11 Inspecting steering wheel for axial play
diagrams.description: Checking for 0 mm axial play along the column shaft axis at the steering wheel.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: When steering jacket shaft is crushed, axial play occurs.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-12 Installing steering column assembly
diagrams.description: Installation diagram of steering column assembly detailing mounting points 1-7 and tightening torques A through F.
measurements_and_specs: A (Lower joint to rubber coupling): 2.3 to 2.7 kg-m (17 to 20 ft-lb)
B (Steering column clamp): 0.8 to 1.1 kg-m (5.8 to 8.0 ft-lb)
C (Jacket tube bracket to dash panel): 0.54 to 0.74 kg-m (3.9 to 5.4 ft-lb)
D (Rubber coupling securing bolt): 1.7 to 2.0 kg-m (12 to 14 ft-lb)
E (Lower joint to pinion gear): 4 to 5 kg-m (29 to 36 ft-lb)
F (Steering wheel nut): 4 to 5 kg-m (29 to 36 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Tighten bolts and nuts correctly and securely to specified torques. Make sure no undue stress is applied to rubber coupling.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-13 Lining up slit with punched mark
diagrams.description: Aligning universal joint slit with punch mark on the top end of the upper steering shaft.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Line up the slits of universal joints with the punched mark located on the top end of upper steering shaft.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-14 Removing steering lock securing screws
diagrams.description: Location of two headless self-shear screws securing the steering lock housing to the steering jacket tube.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Break two self-shear type screws with a drill or other proper tool. Upon installation, cut off screw heads.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-15 Cross-section of rack-and-pinion and side rod assembly
diagrams.description: Comprehensive cutaway illustration showing internal construction and callouts 1 through 21 of the rack-and-pinion steering gear and side rod linkage.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Backlash is held to 0 mm (0 in) by the retainer and retainer spring.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-16 Loosening bolts securing lower joint assembly
diagrams.description: Loosening coupling bolts connecting the lower joint shaft to the rubber coupling.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 1.7 to 2.0 kg-m (12 to 14 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect lower joint from steering column at rubber coupling.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-17 Disconnecting lower joint from pinion
diagrams.description: Disconnecting lower joint pinch clamp from the steering pinion shaft in the engine compartment.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 4 to 5 kg-m (29 to 36 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Loosen bolt securing lower joint assembly to pinion, and then remove lower joint assembly from engine compartment.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-18 Removing outer ball stud nut
diagrams.description: Removing the side rod outer ball stud nut and cotter pin at the steering knuckle arm.
components: Side rod outer ball stud nut

callouts.1: Side rod outer ball stud nut

measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 5.5 to 7.6 kg-m (40 to 55 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use Ball Joint Puller HT72520000 to detach ball studs from knuckle arms.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-19 Removing bolts securing housing to suspension member
diagrams.description: Removing bolts and lock nuts securing steering gear housing mounting brackets to the front suspension member.
measurements_and_specs: Bolt to welded nut tightening torque: 2.6 to 3.0 kg-m (19 to 22 ft-lb)
Lock nut tightening torque: 3.1 to 3.5 kg-m (22 to 25 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove bolts securing steering gear housing to suspension member.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-20 Removing clamps
diagrams.description: Removing gear boot clamp and dust cover clamp from the steering gear boot.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove both left and right clamps.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-21 Disconnecting side rod assembly
diagrams.description: Unthreading side rod inner socket assembly from the end of the rack shaft.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Do not disassemble side rod assembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-22 Removing adjust lock nut
diagrams.description: Loosening adjust lock nut and unthreading the retainer adjust screw from gear housing.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove retainer spring and steering gear retainer after removing screw.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-23 Removing oil seal
diagrams.description: Prying the pinion shaft oil seal out from the top of the gear housing.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Replace oil seal every disassembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-24 Removing bolts and housing cover
diagrams.description: Removing bolts, pinion housing cover, and pinion adjust shims from the steering gear housing.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Save shims for preload adjustment upon reassembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-25 Pressing pinion bearing out of pinion shaft
diagrams.description: Pressing the ball bearing off the pinion shaft using a hydraulic/mechanical press.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Properly support pinion to avoid damaging gear teeth.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-26 Rack-and-pinion and side rod components
diagrams.description: Exploded view diagram of complete steering rack, pinion gear, housing, boots, and side rod linkage with callouts 1 through 22.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Thoroughly clean all parts in cleaning solvent and blow dry before inspection.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-27 Cross-section of outer ball joint
diagrams.description: Internal cross-section of the outer tie rod ball joint showing callouts 1-6 and clearance specification.
measurements_and_specs: Clearance (axial play): 0.1 to 0.5 mm (0.004 to 0.020 in)
Swinging torque: 0.8 to 1.5 kg-m (5.8 to 10.8 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Measure swinging torque and axial play. Replace when values are not within specified range.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-28 Side rod inner ball joint
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional view of the inner side rod ball socket assembly with callouts 1-8.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Check inner ball joint for play. If ball stud is worn and axial play is excessive or joint is hard to swing, replace as a complete unit.

diagrams.caption: Retainer spring dimensions
diagrams.description: Dimensional sketch of retainer spring showing 21 mm (0.83 in) outside diameter and 19.6 mm (0.772 in) free length.
measurements_and_specs: Load x length: 20 kg (44 lb) x 16.3 mm (0.642 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Inspect spring free length and load before reassembly.

diagrams.caption: Side rod spring dimensions
diagrams.description: Dimensional sketch of side rod inner spring showing 8 mm (0.31 in) diameter and 19.0 mm (0.748 in) free length.
measurements_and_specs: Load x length: 40 kg (88 lb) x 17.0 mm (0.669 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Inspect side rod spring free length and load before reassembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-29 Pressing bearing onto pinion gear
diagrams.description: Pressing the ball bearing squarely onto the pinion gear shaft using an arbor press.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Press bearing onto pinion gear until firmly seated.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-30 Measuring protruding portion of rack
diagrams.description: Measuring protruding length of rack bar from housing end with vernier calipers to establish 87.4 mm (3.441 in) center.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Make sure that rack protrudes by the same amount from both ends of housing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-31 Inserting pinion assembly
diagrams.description: Inserting pinion assembly into housing with the groove on the pinion serration directed upward while meshing teeth.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Properly mesh pinion with rack, and insert pinion assembly with the groove on the pinion serration part directed upward.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-32 Measuring protruding portion of rack
diagrams.description: Re-measuring rack protrusion from housing after pinion insertion to verify equal 87.4 mm (3.441 in) extension.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Make sure again of the length protruding from both the left and right sides of housing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-33 Fitting oil seal
diagrams.description: Fitting the pinion shaft oil seal into the upper pinion bore of the gear housing.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Fit oil seal and make sure pinion rotates smoothly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-34 Locking retainer lock nut
diagrams.description: Locking the retainer adjusting screw lock nut while holding the adjusting screw at the backed-off position.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 4 to 6 kg-m (29 to 43 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Fully tighten adjusting screw and then back it off 20 to 25 degrees. Tighten retainer lock nut to 4 to 6 kg-m.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-35 Area to which liquid sealant is applied
diagrams.description: Sectional view of the steering gear housing showing retainer float play (0.09 mm / 0.0035 in), callouts 1-12, and liquid sealant application area 'A'.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Apply suitable liquid sealant around lock nut at 'A'.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-36 Measuring pinion rotary torque
diagrams.description: Measuring pinion rotary torque using a torque gauge on the pinion serration shaft.
measurements_and_specs: Pinion rotary torque: Less than 20 kg-cm (17 in-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Measure torque required to keep pinion and rack in motion.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-37 Measuring rack force to pull
diagrams.description: Measuring force required to pull rack at neutral position using a spring scale.
measurements_and_specs: Rack force to pull at neutral position: 14 to 17 kg (31 to 37 lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Re-adjust retainer adjusting screw as necessary to obtain proper torque.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-38 Fitting side rod assembly to rack
diagrams.description: Fitting side rod inner socket onto rack end with inner spring and spring seat.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Apply recommended grease to sliding surfaces of side rod inner socket and spring seat. Boot must be positioned toward ball stud end.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-39 L-mark
diagrams.description: Identification L-mark stamped on the left side rod assembly.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Side rod assembly for the left side has an L-mark. No mark is used for the right side.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-40 Tightening lock nut
diagrams.description: Tightening the inner socket lock nut against the rack end using two wrenches.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 8 to 10 kg-m (58 to 72 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Screw inner socket portion until ball seat reaches rack end, then tighten lock nut securely.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-41 Measuring swinging torque
diagrams.description: Measuring swinging torque of the inner side rod ball joint with a spring scale.
measurements_and_specs: Swinging torque: 0 to 0.5 kg-m (0 to 3.6 ft-lb)
Axial play: 0 to 0.05 mm (0 to 0.0020 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Measure swinging torque and axial play upon completion of side rod assembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-42 Measuring rack stroke
diagrams.description: Measuring rack stroke from lock to lock using vernier calipers: 60.7 mm (2.390 in).
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Verify full stroke of 60.7 mm (2.390 in) without interference.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-43 Tightening boot clamp
diagrams.description: Tightening boot clamp screw until the specified lug gap clearance of 2 mm (0.08 in) is reached.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Tighten inside boot clamp securely. Boot should be neither too inflated nor too elongated.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ST-44 Adjusting side rod length
diagrams.description: Sectional view of side rod length adjustment showing 37.9 mm (1.492 in) setting from stopper nut to ball stud center.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 8 to 10 kg-m (58 to 72 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Adjust side rod length both left and right, and tighten steering stopper nuts to specified torque.

diagrams.caption: Steering wheel puller (ST27180001 / J 25726)
diagrams.description: Steering wheel puller tool ST27180001 (Kent-Moore J 25726) featuring puller yoke, center bolt, and two side anchor bolts.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use to pull steering wheel hub off splined shaft without hammer impact.

diagrams.caption: Ball joint remover (HT72520000)
diagrams.description: Ball joint remover HT72520000 lever type tool with forcing screw and pivot pin marked PAT. P.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Insert between side rod ball stud and knuckle arm, tighten bolt to separate ball stud.
